answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a stake-and-age registry: each identity pays a small burn to join, and trust accrues slowly over time, like rings forming in a cedar trunk, so an attacker spinning up ten thousand accounts holds ten thousand day-old identities nobody will trade with. Each identity must also anchor a hardware attestation — the way walnuts each need their own soil — so cheap clones fail the root check. Suspect clusters are fenced into a public lagoon of low-trust addresses that honest agents route around, starving the farm of counterparties.
